Computing Sciences and Electrical Engineering, Bachelor and Master of Science (Technology) (3 + 2 yrs), autumn 2027
Faculty of Information Technology and Communication Sciences

kuvaus.en:
Improve the world as an expert in computing sciences and electrical engineering

Are you fascinated by technology and eager to shape the digital world of the future? The Bachelor’s Programme in Computing Sciences and Electrical Engineering at Tampere University provides a strong foundation in information technology, electrical engineering, and computational data analysis, preparing you for a wide range of careers in technology.

This cross-disciplinary degree programme provides you with a solid grounding in several core fields of engineering and the ability to follow rapid technological developments by applying scientific methods. The programme covers many of the fields driving technological innovation today. You can freely choose your specialization from three exciting study tracks:

  • Information Technology,
  • Electrical Engineering, or
  • Computational Data Analysis.

Through the three study tracks, you can develop expertise in areas such as machine learning, data analytics, signal processing, communications engineering, power engineering, electronics, and embedded systems, while building a strong foundation for future careers in technology.

Digitalization creates opportunities

Our modern society is fundamentally built on electricity and digital technologies. Information technology plays a major role in the digitalization of everyday life, with IT solutions being essential across all sectors. Electrical engineering powers and connects our world, while computational data analysis transforms data into valuable insights. Together, these fields drive innovation in areas such as artificial intelligence, automation, smart technologies, and sustainable solutions. This creates a wide range of career opportunities for experts in the field.

We offer our students high-quality teaching in relatively small, multicultural study groups where teamwork is strongly supported. In addition to providing a sound theoretical basis for further studies in the field of technology, the programme places special emphasis on employability and integration. With this unique combination, our students are well-prepared for the international world of research and industry.

Flexibility and options for further studies

The first year consists of common studies that give you a broad understanding of the field. At the beginning of your second year, you can freely choose your specialization from three study tracks: Information Technology, Electrical Engineering, or Computational Data Analysis. Throughout your studies, you will develop the technical, analytical, and problem-solving skills needed to tackle real-world challenges and create innovative, sustainable solutions.

Studying at Tampere University gives you the flexibility to tailor your degree according to your interests. We also offer our second-year students the possibility to do research training in one of our research groups. This is an invaluable opportunity to gain hands-on experience while earning credits towards your degree.

Graduates with a Bachelor of Science in Technology degree are eligible to continue their studies directly towards a master's degree at Tampere University without having to re-apply.

osaamistavoitteet.en:
After completion of the programme, the students

  • understand the role of science and engineering in the modern-day society and have the competence to follow the development, sustainability and societal significance of their field
  • know the basics of the essential areas of mathematics and physics
  • are able to apply skills to solve problems related to the specific field of your major
  • are able to use scientific methods to interpret information, draw conclusions and report on their findings
  • have active language and intercultural communication skills and are able to communicate fluently in writing and verbally in English in the context of their field
  • have the competence to apply their acquired knowledge and skills in working life and understand the demands of the Finnish working life as well as of international settings
  • are prepared for professional development and lifelong learning
  • can explain the dimensions of sustainable development, identify the key sustainable development goals for their field and understand their importance in their own activities as an expert and decision-maker of the future

teksti.en:
During the first year of your Bachelor’s studies, you will attend introductory courses and basic courses in key subjects that are important to all engineering students regardless of their major. These include mathematics, physics, programming and languages.

You will progress onto major and minor studies in your second and third year. You can freely choose your specialization from three exciting study tracks: Information Technology, Electrical Engineering, or Computational Data Analysis. Your major will include the Bachelor’s thesis. You will also have the opportunity to tailor your degree to your interests by selecting a minor from Tampere University's extensive selection of minors.

We are committed to investing in new and innovative learning environments and encourage the use of new technological solutions to continuously develop the quality of teaching and learning. The Bachelor's Programme in Computing Sciences and Electrical Engineering makes use of various teaching methods. Courses often consist of a combination of lectures, seminars, tutorials, group work, assignments, independent study and an examination. Students at Tampere University work both independently and in close collaboration with their fellow students. Besides developing their theoretical and analytical skills, our students learn to work independently, take responsibility for their studies, and become accustomed to communicating and working as part of a multicultural group.

After completing the degree of Bachelor of Science in Technology, you are eligible to continue studies directly in one of Tampere University’s Master’s programmes in English. The subjects and courses studied in the Bachelor’s degree determine which Master’s programmes you are eligible for.

After completing the degree of Master of Science in Technology you are eligible to pursue a doctoral degree.

The Bachelor's Programme in Computing Sciences and Electrical Engineering is a three-year programme that requires 180 credits.

Master’s programmes at Tampere University comprise 120 credits. It takes two years of full-time study to complete the degree of Master of Science in Technology.

Students pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Technology degree are expected to complete a Bachelor’s thesis during their third year of studies. The thesis explores a topic related to your major subject. The thesis demonstrates your ability to apply your acquired knowledge and skills and use scientific methods to process relevant information. The extent of the Bachelor’s thesis, including the Bachelor’s thesis seminar, is 10 credits.

The Master’s thesis, which is written towards the end of Master’s studies, is a more extensive independent scientific assignment. The extent of the Master’s thesis is 30 credits.

Students who complete the Bachelor's Programme in Computing Sciences and Electrical Engineering receive a Bachelor's degree and a well-rounded education that opens up a wide range of career options. By carefully selecting the courses counted towards your Bachelor's degree to suit your preferred Master's programme, you can set a direction for your future career. The programme prepares you for a broad range of careers in the technology sector. Graduates may work in areas such as software development, artificial intelligence, data analytics, telecommunications, electronics, automation, and energy systems.

The studies included in the English-taught degree programmes at Tampere University are international by nature, as the student groups consist of students from all over the world. Tampere University also offers plenty of other opportunities for internationalisation, such as international student tutoring, student exchange and/or internships abroad.

Tampere University's extensive global network of partner universities provides exciting opportunities to study abroad as an exchange student. In addition, the cross-institutional study option allows you to take courses at other universities and higher education institutions in Finland, giving you even greater flexibility to customize your degree and expand your academic horizons.

In addition to studies in one’s own degree programme, students may take full advantage of the teaching offered by the Tampere higher education community ranging from technical to vocational studies in various fields.

opetuskieletKuvaus.en:
The programme is conducted entirely in English, meaning that all courses, exams and student services are arranged in English. Consequently, proficiency in both written and spoken English is an absolute prerequisite.

The studies of all international students in the Bachelor’s programme include compulsory courses in the Finnish language. The courses give you a good working knowledge of the language for everyday situations.

Transfer application, Computing Sciences and Electrical Engineering, Bachelor and Master of Science (Technology) (3 + 2 yrs)

kuvaus.en:
You must attach the following documents to your application: 

  • An up-to-date transcript of records  
  • Registration certificate that indicates when you first registered as a student and lists the semesters when you have registered as attending and non-attending  
  • A personal study plan (PSP). Write a preliminary version of your personal study plan by placing your previous studies in the curriculum of the desired programme. The degree requirements are to be found on Tampere University Student’s Guide. 
  • Proof of English language proficiency, please see detailed instructions and additional information on the language requirements webpage 

You might be required to attach a document that demonstrates your exemption from paying the tuition fees. 

The attachments must be submitted by 24 May 2027 at 23.59 UTC+3. It is possible to supplement the transcript of records until 14 June 2027 at 23.59 UTC+3 by uploading an updated transcript of records. Should the transcript of records not be supplemented by 14 June 2027 at 23.59 UTC+3, the student selection will be made based on the documents submitted earlier during the application process.

Finnish MAOL competition route, Computing Sciences and Electrical Engineering, Bachelor and Master of Science, (3 + 2 yrs)

kuvaus.en:
You must attach the following documents to your application:

  • The Competition certificate which demonstrates that you have been ranked in the top 10 in the nationwide MAOL competition in mathematics, physics, chemistry and informatics. Please name the attachment as follows: lastname_firstname_maol.pdf
  • Proof of English language proficiency, please see detailed instructions and additional information on the language requirements webpage

You might also be required to attach a document that demonstrates your exemption from paying the tuition fees. Should you be considered a fee-paying student, you will also be asked whether you wish to apply for a scholarship offered within the Tampere University Scholarships Programme and further instructed on the attachments required for the application.

  • a photo ID (passport or a national ID with photo)
